questions.question: The service air line connects to the:
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves. These valves allow the trailer brakes to apply quickly.

questions.question: Before driving, check that air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
Closing the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
Disconnecting air supply lines and listening for escaping air.
Rolling each trailer down a hill and testing the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the rear shut-off valves and listening for escaping air.
questions.explanation: Before driving, make sure air reaches all trailers. Wait for air pressure to build. Send air to both the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: If color-coded, what color shows emergency or supply lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines use color codes to help drivers avoid mistakes when connecting them. Blue marks service lines. Red marks emergency lines.

questions.question: The tractor protection valve:

options.text: Makes sure the engine has enough oil.
Keeps the truck from going too fast.
Keeps air in the truck brakes if the trailer leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the truck brakes if the trailer leaks.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve protects the truck's air brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. It closes automatically when pressure drops too low.

questions.question: When using ABS brakes, you should:

options.text: Press the brake pedal harder than normal.
Press the brake pedal as you normally would.
Press the brake pedal lighter than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: When using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would with a normal brake system.

questions.question: When driving slower than 40 mph, keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, leave one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same rule and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop than smaller ones.

questions.question: Emergency air lines are usually marked with the color:
questions.explanation: Service air lines are marked blue. Emergency air lines are marked red.

questions.question: To help prevent rollovers, you should:

options.text: Keep the load near the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.explanation: To reduce rollover risk, keep cargo as low as possible in the trailer. Also take curves and turns slowly.

questions.question: Trailers with low clearance underneath are difficult to drive:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings can be hard to cross with a low-clearance trailer. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers have the most difficulty crossing raised railroad crossings.

questions.question: Loss of air pressure in the emergency line will cause:

options.text: The tractor protection valve to close.
The rear trailer to detach from the combination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve to close.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve protects the trailer's braking system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. When air pressure in the emergency line drops, the tractor protection valve opens and the emergency trailer brakes activate.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel first?

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to go.
In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing without a trailer, turn the wheel in the direction you want to go. When backing with a trailer, turn the wheel in the opposite direction first. Once the trailer starts to turn, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: The emergency air line supplies air to the:
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) does two things. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, the trailer may:
questions.explanation: If weight is placed mainly on one side of a trailer, the trailer may lean to the side. This increases the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
Prevents the trailer from being accidentally released.
Prevents the vehicle from going too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak. The valve closes automatically if pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Are easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are usually heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. Because of this, they require more driving skill.

questions.question: Trailers built before 1975:

options.text: Do not need to have spring brakes.
Are not allowed on public roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not need to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: Keeping cargo centered on a rig can:
questions.explanation: A rollover is more likely if cargo is loaded unevenly in a rig. Keep a load as centered as possible to help prevent a dangerous rollover.

questions.question: When testing ____, apply your vehicle's brakes with the hand control while moving forward slowly.
questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, make sure the braking system has normal air pressure and release the parking brake. Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control. If the trailer service brakes work correctly, you will feel them activate.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when drivers:
questions.explanation: A rollover happens when a driver takes a turn at too high a speed. Take turns and curves slowly and safely.

questions.question: When entering or crossing traffic while driving a combination vehicle, it is especially important that you:

options.text: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
Expect other drivers to make room for your vehicle.
Wait for other drivers to wave you into their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure there is enough space for your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space on the road than other vehicles. When entering or crossing traffic, make sure there is a large enough gap for you to do so safely.
